---
title: "Listings in Quarto"
---

## What Is a Listing?

A Quarto listing is a structured collection of items that Quarto can display as a table, grid, or custom list. Listings are useful when a website contains repeated content such as projects, blog posts, reports, or portfolio pieces.

## Why Listings Are Useful for a Portfolio

Listings make a portfolio easier to maintain because each project can be stored as its own document. Instead of manually rebuilding a homepage every time a project changes, the website can collect project metadata and display it consistently.

Typical listing metadata includes a title, description, date, image, categories, and a link to the full project.

## Example Configuration

The following YAML can be placed in a page such as `projects.qmd`:

```yaml
listing:
  contents: projects
  type: grid
  categories: true
  sort: "date desc"
  fields: [image, title, description, date, categories]
```

This configuration tells Quarto to find project files in the `projects` folder, display them in a grid, show categories, and place the newest projects first.

## Best Practices

- Use consistent metadata across all project files.
- Write descriptions for the audience, not only for the creator.
- Use meaningful categories so visitors can filter projects.
- Keep project titles short and specific.
- Check the listing on both desktop and mobile layouts.

Listings turn a collection of separate files into an organized, scalable portfolio. This is especially valuable as the number of projects grows.
